title: KV prefetch profiling check-ins (Jun 07, 2026)
content:
Sprint context and goal:
- Sprint 31 focus: reduce p95 generation latency for long-context workloads (32k tokens) while keeping unit GPU token-cost stable. Primary lever this week: aggressive KV prefetch + minor kernel fusion for rotary/kv path.

Attendees:
- Anika (owner), Marco, Keisha, Daniel, Lina, Omar (observability consult)

Summary of work done this week:
1) Prefetch profiler runs (internal harness):
   - Baseline (master): p50=58ms, p95=310ms, mean GPU utilization 62%, KV cache hit-rate 86% for our 32k test shards.
   - Prefetch-v1 (naive async prefetch with 4 outstanding fetches): p50=52ms, p95=240ms, KV hit-rate 91%, but end-to-end memory jitter increased -> 10% OOM risk on 80GB nodes at 2x concurrency.
   - Prefetch-v2 (adaptive window + backpressure): p50=53ms, p95=205ms, KV hit-rate 93%, memory stable; average batch size increased by 8% improving throughput.
   - Notes: v2 wins for p95 and hit-rate; we need graceful degradation for low memory hosts.

2) Kernel change: fused rotary + kv-index lookup patch (PR #842)
   - Microbenchmarks show 6-8% per-token throughput improvement for causal decode on A100, ~3% on H100 (higher memory movement).
   - Combined with prefetch-v2, decoding latency reduced (p95 ~190ms in synthetic replay).
   - Risk: pointer aliasing in a narrow codepath caused a transient correctness failure in one internal model (fixed in branch). Added unit test that replays kv index shapes.

3) Batching adjustments:
   - Continuous batching window increased from 8ms -> 12ms for long-context workload to allow larger coalesced batches. Observed 12% throughput boost on 32k streams, but p50 slightly increased ~2ms for small requests.
   - Decided to keep 12ms for dedicated pools serving long-context customers; default hosted API remains 8ms. Configurable via route policy.

Incidents and open issues:
- Memory jitter with prefetch-v1 created rare OOMs on multi-tenant test clusters. Root cause: no backpressure when kernel queue fills (ticket JIRA-RT-1298). Mitigated by prefetch-v2 which adds queue depth sensing.
- Intermittent regression in model X where tokens in the last KV block were occasionally dropped during fast-swap. Reproduced, patched, PR in review (JIRA-RT-1301).
- Tracing: some traces did not show prefetch spans due to missing instrumentation in fast-path; follow-up to add lightweight spans in runtime (owner: Omar).

Decisions made:
- Merge strategy: land prefetch-v2 behind a feature flag on dedicated and a/b test on two hosted zones for 48 hours. (Owner: Marco)
- Kernel fused rotary patch to be canaried on Dedicated with trace-level checks enabled for the next rollout. If error rate >0.1% revert automatically. (Owner: Keisha)
- Keep batching window 12ms for Dedicated long-context pools; add explicit config toggle in console. (Owner: Lina)

Action items (owner + ETA):
- Marco: push feature-flagged prefetch-v2 to canary clusters, run 48h soak (ETA 2026-06-09).
- Keisha: finish kernel PR tests, add pointer aliasing guard, update kernel perf microbench (ETA 2026-06-08).
- Daniel: add lightweight prefetch spans to tracing, integrate with alerting for missing spans (ETA 2026-06-10).
- Lina: console toggle for batching window + docstring for route policy (ETA 2026-06-11).
- Anika: consolidate perf numbers and write short runbook for rollback criteria (ETA 2026-06-09).

Small experiments to iterate next week:
- Prefetch window auto-tune: test heuristics that shrink the prefetch window under memory pressure during bursts.
- Hybrid caching: keep a tiny LRU of hot KV blocks on-host for ultra-low latency repeated prefixes (memory budget experiment).
- Quantized KV blocks: evaluate 8-bit packed storage for cold segments to reduce mem-footprint.

Questions for the group / discussion items:
- Acceptable p50 trade-off for Dedicated long-context customers if p95 improves by >20%? Ops noted some customers prioritize p95.
- Should we expose prefetch aggressiveness as API-level config or keep it internal? Security/Support weigh in on complexity.

Useful links and artifacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/842
- Trace example: https://console.redwood.ai/sessions/trace/5f4a2b
- Tickets: JIRA-RT-1298, JIRA-RT-1301

Conclusion:
Prefetch-v2 + kernel fusion shows promising p95 wins with acceptable memory behavior in Dedicated pools. Next 48h canary + tracing will determine if we flip feature flags more broadly. Focus for next week: monitoring + automated rollback hooks, lightweight tracing, and the hybrid caching memory-budget experiment.

Notes to self (informal):
- Remember to add the new unit test to CI that uses long-context model replay; intermittent kv-drop reproduction depends on order of small writes.
- Check with infra re: extra swap threshold on 80GB hosts to reduce OOM noise during soak.

Meeting end: 2026-06-07 11:15 PDT
